title: Hosted API - embeddings & rerank demo — KryptonSearch
action_items: Rafael Gomez|Provide sample dataset and query logs|2026-11-20
Maya Li|Run hosted embeddings baseline and share latency/cost estimates|2026-11-20
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-16
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jason Park (Redwood AE), Maya Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (KryptonSearch - Head of Search), Ethan Cole (SRE), Rafael Gomez (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for search relevance. Discussed integration path, sample query/embedding flow, latency/cost tradeoffs, security (SOC2, SSO, data retention), and POC next steps. Customer to share dataset and logs; Redwood to send pricing and run a baseline.

Topics:
- Embedding endpoint behavior and vector size choices
- Rerank endpoint integration patterns (embedding + rerank or embedding-only retrieval)
- Console walkthrough: monitoring per-query latency / cost
- Security: SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS
- POC scope and timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jason: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Jason from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Maya, our systems SE.
[00:08] Maya: Hi all, hi Priya, Ethan, Rafael. We'll keep this tight — demo plus discussion then next steps.
[00:15] Priya: Great thanks, we are mainly interested in improving relevance for site search and reducing bad rerankings. We tried tweakers in-house but cost is spiking.
[00:26] Rafael: Yeah, and we have a big catalogue, lots of short product descriptions, and long support articles. Latency is key — our SLO is ~200ms p95 for search experience.
[00:36] Jason: Perfect, that's helpful. Quick qual — are you currently doing embeddings + ANN store, or more of an Elastic/OpenSearch approach?
[00:44] Priya: We use OpenSearch right now for the first pass, with cosine sim in a custom ranking stage. We also experimented with Pinecone for a small subset.
[00:53] Ethan: Infrastructure is AWS, EKS cluster, and some on-prem data for compliance reasons.
[01:00] Maya: Ok great. For today's flow we'll show hosted embeddings endpoint, then rerank endpoint which takes an initial candidate list + embeddings and returns a relevance score. We'll demo Console traces and cost estimates too.
[01:14] Jason: Important note — hosted API means your data is sent to Redwood's hosted runtime; we have privacy modes and retention controls that we can scope in the POC.
[01:24] Priya: Can you remind me about SOC2 and KMS options? We need to bring this to security.
[01:30] Maya: Yes, we are SOC2 Type II certified; we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments, and for hosted we offer envelope encryption and audit logs. I'll drop the SOC2 pack after.
[01:40] Rafael: Sounds good — also need to confirm data residency EU for some customers.
[01:45] Maya: We have EU regions available; we'll include region routing in the POC.

[02:00] Demo start — screen share (Console)
[02:03] Maya: Ok I'm sharing my screen. This is the Redwood Console — per-model dashboards, latency histograms, token cost breakdowns. On the left is the model catalog; for embeddings we recommend our 1536-d and 512-d profiles depending on recall requirements.
[02:23] Priya: Do you expose the dimension? We typically use 768 dims currently.
[02:28] Maya: Yes, you pick model variant. 768 is common; tradeoffs are precision vs token/compute cost. For shortest latencies you might pick a smaller dimensional model or quantized variant.
[02:39] Rafael: When you say quantized, is that always safe for rerank? We have concerns about quality regressions.
[02:46] Maya: Good question. Quantization can slightly change embedding geometry; for reranking we recommend running an evaluation set — Redwood Optimize can flag regressions against your golden queries. In the POC we'll run A/B evals.

[03:10] Maya (typing): I'll call the hosted embeddings endpoint now with a sample product description.
[03:17] [03:17] Maya: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-768","input":"Wireless noise cancelling headphones with long battery"}'
[03:30] (partial transcription glitch)
[03:32] Priya: Sorry what was the exact endpoint path?
[03:35] Jason: It's /v1/embeddings, payload is text array. The response returns a vector — we return a base64 or JSON array depending on SDK.
[03:45] Rafael: How big is the vector payload — like is it 768 floats? Any recommended compression?
[03:50] Maya: Yes typically 768 floats. We support float32 and quantized int8 variants; we can also store compressed base64 to reduce transfer size.

[04:10] Maya: Now for rerank — we'll simulate a top-k from OpenSearch then call /v1/rerank with query + candidate docs + their embeddings.
[04:22] [04:22] Maya: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"model":"rwd-rerank-v1","query":"best headphones for travel","candidates":[{"id":"123","embedding":[...]},{"id":"456","embedding":[...]}]}'
[04:40] Ethan: So the rerank endpoint accepts embeddings inline — can we pass only doc ids and let Redwood fetch embeddings from your cache?
[04:47] Maya: Right now the simplest path is to pass embeddings; but we can store embeddings server-side as a cache keyed by doc id during the POC. We also offer prefix/KV cache for repeated queries to reduce compute.
[04:58] Rafael: Is that the KV cash — I mean KV cache — sorry transcription — how long do you keep cached items?
[05:04] Maya: We can TTL them per deployment; in hosted defaults are short, but POC can request longer TTLs.

[05:30] Priya: Latency — can you show p95 numbers for embeddings + rerank for small batch?
[05:37] Maya: Sure, switching to traces. For rwd-embed-768 on our hosted prod region, single request embedding is ~60-80ms p50 and ~120-180ms p95 depending on load; rerank latency depends on number of candidates, typically 30-80ms p95 for top-10 if embeddings are provided.
[05:55] Jason: So combined embedding + rerank sequentially you'd be in the ~200-300ms p95 range; we can optimize by computing doc embeddings offline and caching.
[06:08] Priya: That's close to our SLO, we need to lower p95. Thoughts?
[06:13] Maya: Options: precompute doc embeddings and store them in your ANN store, do hybrid search (OpenSearch for candidate generation then rerank), or use Dedicated instances with lower tail latency. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization profile that keeps quality within tolerance while reducing cost.
[06:30] Rafael: How does batching affect tail latency — won't it increase p95?
[06:34] Maya: Continuous batching improves throughput and reduces cost per token, but for strict p95 you can set max latency buckets or route to a low-latency pool. For dedicated, we can give stricter tail guarantees.

[07:00] Priya: On the integration side, our team wants minimal changes — i'd prefer passing doc ids and let your system handle embeddings. That reduces engineering overhead.
[07:09] Maya: We can support that pattern in the POC by running an ingestion job that uploads embeddings to Redwood's cache (or to a private store if you go Private deployment). For hosted, we will store those only for the POC TTL and handle eviction.
[07:21] Ethan: From a security perspective, what about SSO and audit logs?
[07:25] Jason: We support SAML SSO for Console access, RBAC, and per-request audit logs; we'll provide the security packet including SOC2 and our data handling.
[07:34] Priya: Ok, please include retention policy and EU region notes.

[08:00] Live Q&A / edge cases
[08:03] Rafael: If we use your rerank endpoint, can we run constrained rerank that only reorders existing candidates without introducing new docs?
[08:10] Maya: Yes, rerank just scores and orders candidates you provide. We don't introduce external docs in rerank stage.
[08:16] Priya: What about hallucination for long docs? Our support articles are long.
[08:20] Maya: For long docs we recommend chunking and hybrid retrieval then rerank. Rerank uses semantic similarity; hallucination is more a generation issue.

[09:00] Integration walkthrough snippet
[09:03] Maya: Example flow: 1) precompute or on-the-fly embeddings 2) ANN candidate retrieval 3) call Redwood rerank with query + candidate embeddings 4) apply business rules and surface top results.
[09:18] Priya: For the ANN store you mentioned — do you have recommendations?
[09:22] Jason: We see customers using Faiss/Pinecone/Weaviate/OpenSearch. If you want minimal infra, hosted + our caching reduces your operational burden.

[10:00] Cost discussion
[10:03] Priya: Cost is a big concern. Can you ballpark token/embed cost?
[10:08] Jason: For hosted embeddings we bill per-embedding unit; rough example for rwd-embed-768: $0.0008 per embed (example) and rerank per candidate might be $0.001 per doc scored — we'll include precise pricing in the SOW; Optimize can show cost tradeoffs for embedding size and quantization.
[10:27] Ethan: Do you do cost caps or alerts?
[10:30] Maya: Yes, Console supports quotas, per-route budgets, and alerts.

[12:00] POC scoping
[12:05] Jason: Proposed POC: 2 weeks baseline, Redwood runs hosted baseline with a sample of queries and your dataset, we measure relevance (NDCG) and latency/cost, then recommend config. Customer provides dataset and query logs, Redwood provides evaluation harness and pricing.
[12:20] Priya: That sounds good. Timeline? We want to show to leadership by Dec 8.
[12:26] Jason: If we kickoff 11/23 we can have a preliminary baseline by 11/30 and a final report by 12/7 to meet your Dec 8 ask.

[15:00] Technical deep dive points (Maya answers)
[15:05] Rafael: How do you ensure consistent embeddings across model versions?
[15:10] Maya: We version models and support pinning; we also provide similarity drift alerts in Optimize if vector distributions shift.
[15:18] Rafael: Any SDKs? We prefer Python.
[15:21] Jason: Yes Python and JS SDKs, plus REST.

[18:00] Questions about Private/Dedicated
[18:04] Priya: If we later need VPC/Private, how disruptive is migration?
[18:09] Maya: We design APIs to be identical. Migration is mainly around network and KMS integration. We can export model configs and keep prompt/rl configs consistent.

[22:00] Console walkthrough continued
[22:05] Maya: Here is the per-route breakdown — tokens, embeddings, rerank calls, and cost per minute. You can filter by model and region.
[22:20] Priya: Useful, thanks. Can you show an eval run?
[22:25] Maya: Switching to evaluation tab — here's an NDCG curve for a previous customer after switching to our rerank. Shows +0.12 NDCG improvement.

[27:00] Objections and clarifications
[27:05] Priya: Our procurement will ask about SLAs — uptime, latency SLO?
[27:12] Jason: For Hosted we provide uptime SLAs on enterprise plans and an optional Dedicated plan for latency SLOs. We'll include specifics in the contract.
[27:20] Ethan: About data deletion — we need a data purge capability post-POC.
[27:25] Maya: We'll provide a one-click purge for POC data and certificate of deletion.

[30:00] Recap and next steps
[30:05] Jason: Quick recap — Redwood to: 1) send SOC2 + security docs and pricing (Jason) 2) Maya to run baseline on hosted with small sample and share latency/cost numbers 3) Rafael to send sample dataset and query logs. Customer to confirm POC kickoff on 11/23.
[30:25] Priya: Confirmed. We'll share dataset by 11/20.
[30:30] Rafael: I'll drop query logs and a small sample of product titles.
[30:34] Maya: We'll aim to return baseline numbers by 11/20 and SOW by 11/18.

[31:00] Closing notes (some cross talk)
[31:03] Priya: Thanks, this was helpful.
[31:05] Jason: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet.

[31:20] Post-call auto-notes (optional)
- Action item: Jason to send pricing + POC SOW (due 2026-11-18)
- Action item: Rafael to provide dataset and logs (due 2026-11-20)
- Action item: Maya to run hosted baseline & share latency/cost (due 2026-11-20)

End of transcript.
